reviewed_version: arXiv:2312.03657v2, 30 May 2025, 35 pages; journal-final equivalence not assumed
paper_title: Multisymplecticity in Finite Element Exterior Calculus
summary: One Major defect in the general reduced-space theorem: one-sided projection need not preserve symmetric penalties. A fully admissible one-element counterexample has bracket -1/210. Two Minor corrections concern BDM trace degree and an XG boundary term. The former Maxwell Minor is withdrawn: the nonsymmetric-tensor example lies outside the source Hodge/symmetry qualification and supports only a scope clarification.

problems.title: The normal-containment branch of Theorem4.21 needs a projection-compatible penalty
problems.location: pp.21,28–29; bounded symmetric penalty assumption, equation(49), Theorem4.21

assumptions.Wh: span(phi) in degree0, phi=x(1-x-y)(2x-1+y); other degrees zero
assumptions.M: piecewise constant scalar traces on the three edges, both approximate trace spaces
assumptions.f: 0, so base solution0 and symmetric derivative0
assumptions.m: 1 on edge and0 on other edges
assumptions.penalty: alpha(v)=v+<t,v>m+<m,v>t on edge, identity elsewhere; bounded symmetric strictly positive

problems.check: Variations (w1,hat_t1,hat_n1)=(phi,0,c*m) and (w2,hat_t2,hat_n2)=(0,m,-m) satisfy all (19a)–(19c): volume pairing vanishes by degree, normal-vs-test pairing by zero average; flux residuals -t and+t orthogonal to M; global zero-boundary test space trivial on one element. Bracket is -c=-1/210.
problems.result: The theorem's general W_nor subset M branch is false even for a strictly positive symmetric penalty. Variations belong to actual linear solution families.
problems.impact: A main claimed class of strongly multisymplectic methods includes a non-multisymplectic member under the stated general penalty assumptions.
problems.counterevidence: The W_tan subset M branch follows from Lemma3.13. Standard commuting scalar/graded penalties used in named examples are not refuted. Theorem3.17 is not refuted because local multisymplecticity fails.
problems.correction: For the normal-containment branch require P*alpha=alpha*P (or symmetry of P*alpha on the relevant trace-difference space), or use a genuinely self-adjoint compressed penalty P*alpha*P.
problems.correction_verification: Self-adjointness gives vanishing skew trace pairing; exact Gram matrix and counterexample integrals/weak residuals checked.

problems.title: The BDM trace degree in Proposition4.6 is one higher than printed
problems.location: p.20, first displayed trace-space identity in Proposition4.6 proof
problems.check: For n=2,r=0, full P1 Lambda1(K) contains x dx, whose trace on y=0 is x dx, not in P0 Lambda1(e). Full P_(r+1) has P_(r+1) facet traces; trimmed P^-_(r+1) has P_r traces.
problems.result: The displayed common P_r trace space is incorrect for the full-polynomial BDM branch.
problems.impact: Local polynomial-degree identity; strong conservation proof still works with the correct full facet product.
problems.counterevidence: Independently specifiable facet traces and jump membership remain valid with the corrected degrees.
problems.correction: Use degree r+1 for full-polynomial BDM and r for trimmed RT, consistently in the following inclusion.

problems.title: The piecewise XG normal correction omits the boundary alpha*z_tan term
problems.check: On exterior boundary, definition3.2 gives Jz_tan=z_tan, so(42b) and the preceding strong expression give check_z_nor=alpha*(z_tan-check_z_tan), not -alpha*check_z_tan. Scalar z_tan=1,check_z_tan=0,alpha=1 yields1, not0.
problems.result: Displayed boundary branch fails the original boundary weak equation for nonzero interior trace.
problems.impact: Local displayed formula; proof of Theorem4.15 retains correct strong expression, so equivalence theorem is not disproved.
